title: Packed token count is not the prefill backend capability boundary
applies_when: A variable-length recurrent-attention wrapper chooses prefill versus recurrence using a packed token count, while the downstream facade also considers sequence count, speculative mode, state dtype or bias layout.
lesson: Compare both dispatch predicates before changing arithmetic or state precision. In FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 KDA, ordinary packed prefill requires total_tokens > num_sequences, not merely total_tokens > 1. Thus [1,1], [1,1,1,1] and padded [2,0] can enter a different implementation than [2] or [1,2]. That implementation can have a narrower FP32 state or 2-D bias contract. Pass host-known sequence metadata to a compatible existing fallback; keep snapshot/checkpoint capability checks aligned with the kernel actually selected. Preserve ordinary FP32 prefill instead of downcasting the state or disabling the whole backend. Test the affected shapes and unchanged multi-token controls in each claimed dtype against an independent output/state reference, including an untouched cache slot.
avoid_when: The inequality is specific to the cited FlashInfer version and ordinary non-speculative KDA path; do not apply it as a universal varlen rule or infer every request has one token from totals alone. New versions may support recurrence's wider state/layout domain. The public native experiment used real leaf adapters and kernels but isolated package entrypoints and dispatcher methods, with a different full dependency set from current SGLang main. It is not official registered-test, full backend, CUDA Graph, server, model, performance or cross-hardware qualification. Passing advice retrieval does not establish better Scout PR yield or research cost.

evidence.note: The ordinary-prefill predicate explicitly uses positive sequence count and packed tokens > sequences, and rejects speculative mode. Source-level capability evidence, not a measured speedup.

Reporter supplies a public FlashInfer reproducer distinguishing FP32/BF16 state and flat/2-D bias. The original serving source had downstream patches; its batch lengths were not captured. Do not equate the sufficient minimal trigger with the original server's exact shape.

Open, unmerged repair of both dispatcher consumers at head ac787b6fdc2d3b530ba1c8a69d0fa74f07f332a3. Ten B300 component comparisons cover five shapes in FP32/BF16; six baseline errors become passes and four ordinary-prefill controls pass both arms. Real native leaves plus isolated host dispatch, not full-package/registered-suite validation.
